gap: No result ChatGPT got states any lab-measured brightness, contrast or colour figure for a laptop screen extender. Notebookcheck measured FOPO's own earlier triple extender at 185 nits centre, 247:1 contrast and 79% sRGB. The one 16-inch extender a lab has measured (Monduo 16 Pro Duo, Notebookcheck) reached 402–430 nits at about 15 W per screen. Meanwhile FOPO claims 100% sRGB for the S788 and lists its brightness as 'being verified'.
standout_why: I compared against the cited FOPO S788 product page, the cited UPERFECT 'best triple screen' blog and our own Dealectric page. The FOPO S788 page has no reviewer data and lists brightness and contrast as 'being verified'. The UPERFECT blog gives only stated specs (FOPO S9G '300 nits', '120% sRGB') and its page has no measured figures. Our page cites Notebookcheck only for its qualitative 'clunky' verdict, with no numbers. The other cited pages are maker and retailer listings (VueXtend Tri 16, Best Buy MagHub Dual, FOPO S11). I could not open them on 2026-11-08, but by their nature they carry maker specs. None of these pages has a named measurement.
decides: This confirms rather than changes the pick. None of the 1920×1200 16-inch candidates has a named lab measurement. What the measurements do show is that extender panels can fall well short of their claims: FOPO's 12-inch measured 79% sRGB and 247:1, and Notebookcheck found the KYY X90A below the maker's stated brightness. So the page can say the shopper should treat '300 nits / 100% sRGB' on the S788, S9G, S11 and MagHub as unverified. If verified brightness matters most, the only lab-measured 16-inch option is the Monduo 16 Pro Duo, and its 2560×1600 panels sit outside the 1920×1200 brief. Notebookcheck's 15 W per screen also supports separate power for a three-panel S788.

findings.label: Measured brightness, contrast and gamut (Notebookcheck, Allen Ngo, published 2022-07-23)
findings.value: 185 cd/m² centre, 177 cd/m² average, 85% distribution; black 0.75 cd/m²; contrast 247:1; 79% sRGB; ΔE ColorChecker 4.59 (0.84 calibrated); no PWM
findings.source_title: FOPO 12-inch triple monitor extender review: Clunky and more fragile than standalone portable monitors – Notebookcheck
findings.note: Measured with Notebookcheck's colorimeter and Calman. This is an older and smaller FOPO model, not the S788. The page prints the minimum as 17.77 cd/m², which conflicts with its grid low of 164.7, so I left the minimum out.

findings.label: Measured max brightness, gamut and battery impact (PCWorld, Mark Hachman, 2022-02-04)
findings.value: Right screen 311 nits, left screen 426 nits at max; 74% sRGB, about 55% AdobeRGB; test-laptop battery fell from 809 min to 181 min with the screens running
findings.source_title: Review: FOPO's 'triple' laptop monitor is a road warrior's dream tool – PCWorld
findings.note: Colorimeter reading per PCWorld. The two panels in one unit differed by 115 nits (426 − 311). The battery figure works out to a drop of about 78%.

findings.label: Measured brightness, contrast and gamut (Notebookcheck, Sebastian Bade, 2023-08-10)
findings.value: Centre 258 / 228 cd/m², average 235 / 210 cd/m² (left/right); contrast 956:1 / 912:1; sRGB 95.4% / 94.8%; ΔE 3.28 / 3.07; no PWM
findings.source_title: KYY X90A dual monitor review – Notebookcheck
findings.note: Notebookcheck says the measured levels were 'below what was stated by the manufacturer'. Price was about US$480 at review.

findings.label: Measured brightness, contrast, gamut, power and weight (Notebookcheck, Christian Hintze, 2023-05-14)
findings.value: Centre 402 / 430 cd/m², average 389 / 422 cd/m²; contrast 1058:1 / 1229:1; sRGB 99.9% / 100%; DCI-P3 97%; about 15 W per display (30 W for both); 1.9 kg; no PWM
findings.source_title: Monduo 16 Pro Duo in review: A built-in triple-monitor setup for laptops – Notebookcheck
findings.note: The only 16-inch extender I found with lab measurements. It advertises 500 nits and measured about 402–430. Its panels are 2560×1600, not 1920×1200. Price was about $799 at review. The left/right split is inferred from the review's table layout.

findings.label: Maker's published display claims (for contrast with the measurements above)

findings.source_title: FOPO S788 16" Triple Laptop Screen Extender
findings.note: Maker page. It lists a regular price of $499.99 alongside a 'sale' price of $999.99, which looks like a listing error.
